Issue Title : Network File Server 2 (NFS-2) Hardware Related Issues
Revision Description
Revised Status Section, Final Action, and the Milestone Section with connector solder joint failures dates.
Applicability
737 MAX airplanes with the NFS serial numbers (S/Ns) mentioned in the Status section below.
Description
737MAX operators have experienced Network File Server (NFS) issues. Currently, there are two known
hardware related issues with the NFS: Solid State Drive (SSD) and Network Extension Device (NED)
Subsystem Processor (NSP) connector failures.
SSD Failure Symptoms:
• Fault Light on the front of the NFS is solid ON for greater than 10 minutes following power-up.
SSD Failure Background:
• Delkin (SSD supplier) failure analysis did not identify root cause.
• Delkin attempted to resolve the issue with a firmware update, which had no positive effect.
The leading hypothesis is that the SSDs are susceptible to power interruptions while they are being written
to.
Connector Solder Joint Failure Symptoms:
The typical failure is a degraded performance of the A429 ACARS Output (output #4). However as the
failure mode progresses, this can become a persistent failure of this output port. In extreme cases, other
A429 and Program Pins may be affected.

Issue Title : Network File Server 2 (NFS-2) Hardware Related Issues
Revision Description
Revised Status Section, Final Action, and the Milestone Section with connector solder joint failures dates.
Applicability
737 MAX airplanes with the NFS serial numbers (S/Ns) mentioned in the Status section below.
Description
737MAX operators have experienced Network File Server (NFS) issues. Currently, there are two known
hardware related issues with the NFS: Solid State Drive (SSD) and Network Extension Device (NED)
Subsystem Processor (NSP) connector failures.
SSD Failure Symptoms:
• Fault Light on the front of the NFS is solid ON for greater than 10 minutes following power-up.
SSD Failure Background:
• Delkin (SSD supplier) failure analysis did not identify root cause.
• Delkin attempted to resolve the issue with a firmware update, which had no positive effect.
The leading hypothesis is that the SSDs are susceptible to power interruptions while they are being written

Connector Solder Joint Failure Symptoms:
The typical failure is a degraded performance of the A429 ACARS Output (output #4). However as the

FLEET TEAM DIGEST
• No Present Leg Fault (PLF) and Real-Time Event (RTE) reports downlinked via ARINC Communications
Addressing and Reporting System (ACARS) datalink.
• No CFM LEAP EEC reports downlinked to ground via ACARS datalink.
• Excessive instances (10 or more over the last 10 flight legs) of Maintenance Message 23-23010 (CMU
HAS NO INPUT FROM NFS-L ON CABIN TERM #1).
• Not affected: PLF and Fault History (FH) reports are downlinked to Loadable Software Airplane Part Library
(LSAPL) via Wireless Network or Gatelink
Not affected: Able to access to the PLF, FH, and Inbound Flight Deck Effects from the Multi-function
Display System (MDS) or Maintenance Laptop
Connector Solder Joint Failure Background:
• Service Related Problem 737MAX-SRP-46-0006 was opened to investigate the NSP Connector issue
• The preliminary investigation indicates the internal Circuit Card Assembly (CCA) connectors are being
exposed to forces greater than design.
• Root Cause of the solder joint failures has been determined.
Status
SSD Status:
• Teledyne Controls selected an alternate supplier for the Solid State Drive (SSD): ATP Electronics.
• ATP Electronics SSD are newer technology with improved firmware and architecture.
• ATP Electronics SSD provide a power protection feature to ensure a graceful shutdown.
• The ATP Electronics SSD built in power protection feature does result with a requirement to fully power
cycle the NFS during manual resets. If using the Circuit Breaker, ensure that it is pulled for a minimum of
three seconds before reapplying power.
• Teledyne Controls replacing Delkin with ATP Electronics SSD on returned units with a failed Delkin SSD.
• Production units (beginning with S/N 47B01090) are being delivered with ATP Electronics SSD. Refer to
the Service Bulletin for applicable serial numbers
• Field returns with replacement SSD are being tracked by Mod Dot and Serial Number.
Teledyne Controls Service Bulletin (SB) SB2247200-46-7 was released for NFS P/N 2247200-01, and lists
the NFS serial number effectivity.
Teledyne will the following service bulletins by the end of 1Q 2021.
Teledyne Controls Service Bulletin (SB) SB2247200-46-12 is released for NFS P/N 2247200-01
Teledyne Controls Service Bulletin (SB) SB2247200-46-15 is released for NFS P/N 2247200-03
Connector Solder Joint Status:
Maintenance Message 23-23010 (CMU HAS NO INPUT FROM NFS-L ON CABIN TERM #1) is effective
for predictive alerting of the connector issue.
Teledyne performed a failure analysis and modified the design to mechanically disconnect the Network
Extension Device (NED) Subsystem Processor (NSP) from the Server Subsystem Processor (SSP)
Module Assembly.
• Root Cause has been established. NSP Connector: The mechanical tolerance stack-up in the NFS and th
dissimilar thermal expansion properties of the epoxy used on the connectors resulted in mechanical stres
causing fractures in the solder terminations between the connector and the printed wiring board.
• Teledyne will the following service bulletins by the end of 1Q 2021.

FLEET TEAM DIGEST
Teledyne SB SB2247200-46-13 supersedes SB2247200-46-9 and is released for NFS PN 2247200-01.
Teledyne SB SB2247200-46-14 is released released NFS PN and 2247200-03.
Interim Action
If NFS exhibits symptoms described in the discussion section, remove the NFS per AMM Task
46-13-01-000-801 (Network File Server Removal) and Replace the NFS per AMM Task 46-13-01-400-801
(Network File Server Installation).
Final Action
Boeing recommends airline operators send failed NFS units back to Teledyne Controls for repair.
Root Cause has been established. on the NSP connector a mechanical tolerance stack-up in the NFS and the
dissimilar thermal expansion properties of the epoxy used on the connectors resulted in mechanical stress
causing fractures in the solder terminations between the connector and the printed wiring board.
